riley: Heads-up PR #799 added an Optimize migration note but CI flagged a couple of infra-y issues: broken link(s) and a snippet that fails the snippet runner.

riley: Broken path points to /optkit/quant-profiles (404). The canonical location is /optimize/quantization.

sam: Which snippet broke?

riley: The Python quant example still uses the old constructor:
```python
from redwood.optimize import QuantProfile
q = QuantProfile(precision='int8', calibrate=True)
```

kevin: Yep, that will fail against SDK >=0.9. API now expects a dtype and a calibrator instance. Minimal compatible example we use in tests:
```python
from redwood.optimize import QuantProfile, DefaultCalibrator
q = QuantProfile(dtype='qint8', calibrator=DefaultCalibrator())
```

kevin: Also drop the `calibrate` kw arg entirely.

mira: Also noticed some runtime YAML samples in the docs still set `kv_cache_enabled: true`. That runtime flag was renamed to `kv_prefetch: auto|on|off`. It's not breaking snippet-exec, but it's confusing.

sam: I'll open a tiny PR that 1) updates /optkit/quant-profiles -> /optimize/quantization, 2) swaps the Python example, and 3) runs a grep/replace for `kv_cache_enabled` -> `kv_prefetch: 'auto'` where appropriate. I'll keep the text edits minimal.

kevin: After that, I'll add a short smoke test at docs/tests/snippets/quant_profile_smoke.py that executes the quant snippet via snippet-exec in CI. That'll catch API drift next time.

riley: Please also add a one-line migration note to the checklist: "SDK <0.9 -> >=0.9: replace QuantProfile(precision=...) with QuantProfile(dtype=...) and use a calibrator object (e.g., DefaultCalibrator) instead of calibrate=True."

ci-bot: PR #799  link-checker: 1 broken link, snippet-exec: 1 failed. Artifacts: https://ci.redwood.example/799/artifacts

sam: PR opened and tagged @kevin for the test. Keeping changes scoped to links/code samples only.

mira: Thanks. If CI still trips after these small fixes we'll hold the docs sync and triage in #release-war-room.

sam: Will ping here with CI rerun results.

kevin: On it  adding the test now and will assert the QuantProfile has a `dtype` attribute so future regressions fail fast.
